resources.string: Shift every chord by the chosen number of semitones (positive = up, negative = down).
Suggest a capo position for this song.\n\nChoose the fretboard voicing the suggestion should optimize for; the recommended capo makes those shapes easiest to play.

Starting from this point, the tempo of playback changes to/by the given amount.

Valid formats:
 • 110 - absolute change
 • +20 - relative change
 • 20% - relative change by percentage
 • 2x - multiplier
 • reset or original - reset back to initial BPM
Starting from this point, the time signature of playback changes to this value.
Starting from this point, the key in which relative chords play will change.\n\nSelect the new key signature from the list below.
Inserts a label which can be used for making loops.\n\nEnter a unique label name (letters, numbers, and underscores only).

From this point on, chord boxes and tabs are shown for a capo on this fret. The key stays the same, but a fretboard voicing plays these shapes, so its notes can change.\n\nEnter a fret from 0 to 12 (0: no capo), or let Suggest pick the easiest one.

Placed at the end of a loop.

To set the beginning of a loop, use a label directive (＋ Insert → Label).
Use '@start' as a special keyword for the beginning of the song.
Tap keys on the piano or type notes below (e.g., C E G or C, E, G). Long-press a key to hear it without selecting it.
Piano keyboard, two octaves from C4
